criteria.criterion: isolated verification prototype (not product code) of the OM-Crypto-v1 PQXDH + Double Ratchet state machine (ADR-0118; SPQR is v2) runs on native and wasm32 with state persistence/reload
criteria.note: PQXDH rev3 + Double Ratchet rev4 (no SPQR). 249 steps, each in a fresh process/instance, 367 messages incl. out-of-order and skipped keys carried across reloads; native, wasm32-wasip1 (wasmtime), alternating native/wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown (Node/V8) produce byte-identical state at every step.

criteria.criterion: deterministic vectors produced by the prototype are consumed by a second independent implementation or checked against upstream KATs
criteria.note: Python (cryptography/OpenSSL + kyber-py) reproduces or verifies 236/236 values: binding chain and 14 negative binding vectors, PQXDH, handshake_id, ML-KEM, DR keys, AEAD inputs, bit-exact AES-GCM-SIV ciphertexts and the HPKE envelope; it rejects a mutated ciphertext and a mutated ML-DSA-65 signature. NIST ACVP ML-KEM-768: 80/80 on libcrux (native+wasi), 80/80 on kyber-py.

criteria.criterion: one-time key material handling and depletion behavior demonstrated without downgrade
criteria.note: 17 checks pass on native, wasip1 and Node: depletion to the signed ML-KEM prekey, single-use deletion, replay rejection, tampered handshake consumes nothing, PQ-less bundle and CT-less initial message refused, epoch rotation with grace and expiry.

criteria.criterion: dependency, licensing and update strategy recorded in an ADR
criteria.note: ADR-0118 (strategy; v1 without SPQR) and ADR-0135 §6 (the v1 dependency set: libcrux ML-KEM/ML-DSA, dalek, RustCrypto; all MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD). Resolved graph licence classes: ['(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0', 'Apache-2.0', 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT', 'BSD-2-Clause OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT', 'BSD-3-Clause', 'MIT', 'MIT OR Apache-2.0', 'Unlicense OR MIT'].

criteria.criterion: no reliance on an unsupported external library API contract
criteria.note: The v1 path depends only on crates.io releases used through their documented public APIs (FIPS 203/204/RFC primitives); spqr and libsignal are gone from the graph. Wire and state encodings are OM-defined (frozen CDDL + ADR-0135), not library-defined.

criteria.criterion: PQXDH DeviceIdentity binding vectors require both Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 over the PQXDH identity/prekey binding and reject either-signature substitution (ADR-0131 rule 1)
criteria.note: 20 Rust checks on three runtimes and 14 negative vectors the Python verifier (OpenSSL Ed25519/ML-DSA-65) also rejects: either half substituted, either half alone, halves split into two entries, prekey/one-time-item/identity-key/signing-key substitution, quarantined device, stale or untrusted ACS head.

criteria.criterion: last-resort PQXDH replay prototype persists an exact per-signed-prekey transcript ledger before acknowledgement, rejects duplicates across crash, and fails closed at the 4096 cap without eviction (ADR-0131 rule 2)
criteria.note: 7 checks: vault commit precedes plaintext release; a failed commit changes and releases nothing; replay after crash+reload rejected; 4096 real handshakes fill an epoch, the 4097th is LastResortExhausted, the first id is still rejected (no eviction), one-time initiations still work, a fresh epoch accepts.

criteria.criterion: AES-256-GCM-SIV payload vectors verify the OM-DR-AEAD-KEY-v1 / OM-DR-AEAD-NONCE-v1 derivation and authenticated header context (ADR-0131 rule 3)
criteria.note: Python recomputes header_hash, K, N and AD for all 16 vector messages and matches every GCM-SIV ciphertext bit-exactly; header and envelope-context tampering are rejected in Rust and Python.

criteria.criterion: MessageRequest HPKE consumes draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 MLKEM768-X25519/HKDF-SHA256/ChaCha20Poly1305 KATs plus OM context vectors; no ad-hoc hybrid implementation (ADR-0131 rule 9)
criteria.note: Official draft-05 vectors (pinned commit + SHA-256): Rust 33 checks on native/wasi/node and Python 33 checks, all pass; the OM info/ticket binding vector is reproduced by Python. The combiner is the draft's CG construction, verified by its KATs, not an OM design.

criteria.criterion: responder binds the inbound PQXDH initiator IK_A to exactly one active, non-quarantined DeviceCredential committed by the trusted relationship ACS head before any secret-key operation, with negative vectors for unknown, route-mismatched, revoked, quarantined, stale, substituted and ambiguous keys checked by the independent implementation (ADR-0136 rule 4, review F-9)
criteria.note: Responder IK_A is checked against the trusted relationship ACS/DeviceCredential before secret-key work. Current selftests and independent Python vectors include route mismatch, stale/revoked/quarantined/substituted/ambiguous cases; focused non-Anthropic GPT-5.6 Sol re-review accepted the remediation.

criteria.criterion: ADR-0135 §7 / ADR-0136 rule 4 responder binding accepted on re-review by a non-Anthropic reviewer (review F-9 reopened V-001)
criteria.note: GPT-5.6 Sol independently accepted the responder-side initiator binding remediation for F-9.

criteria.criterion: ADR-0140 AsyncKeyBundle v1 prototype persists a recipient high-water mark across reload/provider migration, rejects lower-generation replay and equal-generation core equivocation, and rejects one-time-prekey transplantation across device/profile/generation/provider-pool context
criteria.note: 8 focused native/wasip1/Node checks cover same-generation migration across disjoint pools, generation-floor persistence through Device serialization/reload, lower-generation rollback, equal-generation core equivocation, and item transplantation across pool/device/profile/generation. Independent Python consumes refreshed current-tree vectors.

criteria.criterion: SealedDeliveryEnvelope HPKE consumes the OM-Crypto-v1 pinned draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 suite under ADR-0142 route-bound info/AAD and padding buckets, rejects wrong route/key/expiry, and never treats outer open as sender authentication
criteria.note: 15 focused native/wasip1/Node checks plus an independent Python seal/open vector exercise the exact 1216-byte public key, 1120-byte hybrid encapsulation, draft-05 suite, route-bound info, wrapper AAD, all five padding buckets, expiry, wrong route/key, tampering and the sender-authentication boundary. No clear-sender fallback is accepted.

criteria.criterion: [pre-release] independent cryptographic review of the integrated production path
[pre-release] production build provably excludes dev/test CryptoProvider (R-072)
criteria.note: Sketch only: `production` + `insecure-test-rng` is a compile_error!, the production build succeeds, and its rlib contains no InsecureTestRng (the test build's does, as a control).

criteria.criterion: V-001 and V-005 prototypes record crypto and codec costs on native and wasm32 against the budgets; unattainable budgets revised by ADR
criteria.note: V-001 costs recorded on native, wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown (Node/V8) on an Apple M3; no reference low-end device.

independence.authorship: written by a Claude agent; the design package was authored by a ChatGPT design agent and Claude agents; ADR-0117 (proposed) decides whether an AI reviewer counts as independent
limitations: both implementations written by the same AI agent (ADR-0134 §5 accepts language/runtime diversity for pre-engineering)
independence.second_implementation: Python 3 (cryptography/OpenSSL, kyber-py) written from the public specs; different language and different primitive libraries than the Rust side (dalek, libcrux, RustCrypto)
upstream_kat: NIST ACVP-Server ML-KEM-768 internalProjection.json at a pinned commit with SHA-256
